claims.text: JLS 25 describes Java access control as a mechanism that prevents users of a package or class from depending on unnecessary implementation details; accessibility is determined from declaration modifiers and context at compile time.
A Java class has one direct superclass type: Object has none, and a normal class without an explicit extends clause has Object as its direct superclass.
JLS 25 distinguishes overriding by instance methods from hiding by class/static methods and imposes compile-time requirements on overriding relationships.

Same-name methods with signatures that are not override-equivalent are overloaded; method applicability and most-specific selection occur as part of compile-time method invocation processing rather than ordinary run-time overriding lookup.

For ordinary virtual/interface instance invocation, JLS 25 performs dynamic method lookup starting from the actual run-time class of the target object; static invocation needs no target and does not allow overriding, while private methods do not enter ordinary overriding lookup.

A Java class may directly implement one or more interfaces, and Java SE 25 interface method declarations can use abstract, default, static and private/public forms; interfaces are therefore not restricted to abstract method declarations.
